{{short description|Polish mathematician}}
'''Tomasz Łuczak''' (born 13 March 1963 in [[Poznań]])<ref>Joseph A., Mignot F., Murat F., Prum B., Rentschler R. (1994.) [https://books.google.com/books?id=hLrptG7XxvwC&pg=PR43 ''First European Congress of Mathematics Paris, July 6–10, 1992: Vol. 1: Invited Lectures''], Nelson Thornes.</ref> is a Polish [[mathematician]] and [[professor]] at [[Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań]] and [[Emory University]]. His main field of research is [[combinatorics]], specifically [[discrete mathematics|discrete]] [[Mathematical structure|structures]], such as [[random graph]]s, and their [[chromatic number]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Łuczak |first=Tomasz |author-mask=3 |title=The chromatic number of random graphs |journal=Combinatorica |volume=11 |issue=1 |year=1991 |pages=45–54 |doi=10.1007/BF01375472 |s2cid=189917450 |url=http://purl.umn.edu/4809 }}</ref>

Under supervision of [[Michał Karoński]], Łuczak earned his doctorate at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań in 1987.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=154490 }}</ref> In 1991, he received the [[Kuratowski Prize]] and the following year, he was awarded the [[EMS Prize]]. In 1997, he won the prestigious [[Prize of the Foundation for Polish Science]] for his work on the theory of [[discrete mathematics|random discrete structures]].
